ExplanationParts.CorpusEarnedOpening: To make something clear or bring it to light.
EvidenceBody: Chan biographies repeatedly say that someone brings “the great matter,” “the mind-ground,” or “the essentials of mind” to light. One record lists bringing the great matter to light alongside having one's mind-ground opened through mountains and waters and recognizing one's original face through things encountered; the text supplies these neighboring predicates without making them synonyms. A later address states its aim as having each person “directly bring to light one's own fundamental great matter” (直下發明自己本分大事), anchoring direct instruction rather than retrospective biography. Other biographies say “there will certainly be clarification” (必有發明) or that someone was “not greatly clarified” (不大發明). Those result and degree constructions name the outcome of the same bringing-to-light event, not another lexical referent.
